scenarios.text: A flamefang darts in and bites a colonist on the leg. Over the next several in-game hours the colonist's health tab lists only a bite wound that bleeds a little and starts to heal; no venom entry ever appears.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf requires the bite to leave flamefang venom on the colonist, worsening over the hours; a bite that leaves only a wound is the leaf's red.

scenarios.text: A fire-hawk flies off holding a burning twig and drops it one cell beyond the edge of the running grass fire. That cell catches; the burn's own spread had already reached the neighbouring cell a moment earlier, and no other spot far from the front ever ignites where a hawk dropped anything.
scenarios.expect: reject: the drop cell may have been lit by the fire's own spread (named false pass), so nothing shows the hawk starting a new fire ahead of the blaze.

scenarios.text: Grass on a deep-ash pad burns away. Afterwards the burned pad has a dusting of loose ash, but an untouched deep-ash pad beside it, with no fire at all, has banked exactly the same loose ash over the same hours from the drifting ash.
scenarios.expect: reject: the loose ash on the burned pad is ambient drift that would have banked there without any fire (named false pass); the fire leaving loose ash behind it is not shown.

scenarios.text: A furnace-beast stands in the colony. The mod's XML file gives it a body size of 6, but the running game's def inspector shows a body size of 2.4, and the beast is no larger on screen than a muffalo.
scenarios.expect: reject: the leaf requires body size 6 in the running game; reading the size from the XML is a named false pass and an ordinary-sized beast is the red.

scenarios.text: On a cold night with no fire anywhere near the colony, the running game's inspector shows a furnace-beast's body size as 6 and it looms over the colonists. A colonist standing next to it gains a warmth status that a colonist across the map does not have, and the closed room it shelters in reads well above the temperature of an identical empty room next door.
scenarios.expect: accept: a giant at size 6 in the running game that warms anyone near it and heats its room, with no burn outside to explain the heat.

scenarios.text: An ashwallow grazes far from any fire when a heat hit strikes it. It flops onto its side the same way any hurt animal lies down, and its dome sprite shows the whole time, before the hit and after it.
scenarios.expect: reject: the dome sprite drawn all the time, or the animal simply lying down when hurt, are named false passes; nothing shows it curling into its dome because of the heat hit and holding until the hold runs out.

scenarios.text: On arrival a long grass-fire front lights and crosses the map, leaving a black scorched trail. By the end of day two it has burned out. Through day five no flame or smoulder appears anywhere on the map, open grass included.
scenarios.expect: reject: the burn line lights once and never relights, so the map stays dark, which is the leaf's red.

scenarios.text: Ten days into a Pyrelands colony, a census of the living map counts boomalopes and wild healroot from another biome alongside the native cast, and the big predators outnumber the small grazers.
scenarios.expect: reject: a donor animal or plant on the map, and big predators outnumbering grazers, are the leaf's red.

scenarios.text: The grass front reaches a strip of ordinary concrete two cells wide and goes no farther; a smoulder relights in grass right beside the strip and also stops at it. Later a fire-hawk carries an ember and starts a fire six cells past the strip. The architect menu offers no chemfuel firebreak floor.
scenarios.expect: accept: a vanilla paved strip two cells wide stops both the front and a near-side relight, the hawk carrying an ember six cells past it is allowed, and the firebreak floor is gone.

scenarios.text: A patch of ember grass burns black. On day three about a quarter of it shows green shoots; on day seven roughly 60% of it is green again, without any replanting, and the open ground around it is carpeted with grass, not wide bare dirt.
scenarios.expect: accept: ember grass carpets the ground, burns black and is largely green again within about a week, inside his card thresholds (a nearly-all-green week is playtest tuning, not this leaf).

scenarios.text: Black rain falls on a scar only hours old. Half a day later the inspector reads that scar's growth rate the same as an old, wet ash patch that never burned.
scenarios.expect: reject: black rain must add to the fresh-burn bonus (a wet fresh scar reads 190%), and still wiping it within half a day is the leaf's red.

scenarios.text: Within hours of the front passing, scorch-fruit sprouts in the black cells just behind it; none comes up on the unburned ash next to the scar. A colonist picks and eats one and their hunger drops. A fruit left on a shelf rots within a short while.
scenarios.expect: accept: scorch-fruit comes up rapidly in the fresh scar right behind the front, not on unburned ground, feeds a colonist and rots fast.

scenarios.text: In daylight three weather captures are compared side by side. Ash fall and cinderfall are clearly different. Black rain draws as the usual blue-grey streaks of ordinary rain.
scenarios.expect: reject: black rain drawing as blue-grey rain is the leaf's red; each sky must read at a glance as its own.

scenarios.text: A full season passes with weather running normally and only black rain ever falls as wet weather. The biome's weather list, opened in dev mode, still has ordinary rain on it at a low commonality.
scenarios.expect: reject: ordinary rain being on the biome's weather list is the leaf's red, even if it was never chosen in that season.

scenarios.text: A wild ullai herd that arrived on its own walks across the map to graze the patch that burned about two days earlier, passing over the scar the front left that morning and the unburned grass alike.
scenarios.expect: accept: the herd drifts to graze where it burned about two days ago and not on the fresh scar, and it was not spawned on the scar.

scenarios.text: A colonist is ordered to shovel a patch of Pyrelands sand. Each dug cell yields five glass sand and turns to gravel; the same cells offer no second dig order. A reachable non-sand cell next to it offers no dig order at all.
scenarios.expect: accept: five glass sand a cell, leaving gravel, so the patch is finite, and other ground yields nothing.

scenarios.text: A colonist on a cleared pad is bitten twice by a hostile flamefang; within the hour its health tab lists RM_FlamefangVenom, and the severity climbs each hour for six hours. In the control, the same colonist is bitten by a warg of similar size: the health tab lists the bite wound and also a small RM_FlamefangVenom entry, which climbs more slowly.
scenarios.expect: reject: no other bite may carry the venom; the control bite from a non-venomous predator must leave no RM_FlamefangVenom, and here it does, so any bite applies it

scenarios.text: A grassed deep-ash pad is burned while a light ash fall drifts in, and afterwards the pad holds 38 loose-ash filth. The control, the same pad burned under the same light ash fall with fire ash-dusting switched off, holds 35 loose-ash filth.
scenarios.expect: reject: the loose ash must be left by the fire, not ambient drift; the test should be in clear weather, and the dusting-off control holds about the same count, so the ash is drift that would have banked with no fire

scenarios.text: On the map the furnace-beast is drawn far larger than every other animal. Its defs file on disk gives body size 6. The live def query in the running game returns body size 3.2; its sprite is scaled up by the graphic's draw size.
scenarios.expect: reject: the giant must be body size 6 in the running game's def, not the XML file; a live 3.2 is the classic muffalo-class beast, only drawn big

scenarios.text: An ashwallow stands on a pad with no ground fire and is struck once by a heat hit that lights nothing. It lies down on the spot at once. About an in-game hour later it is in its dome stance with the burrow job, and later it gets up and walks off. With the dome switch off, the same hit makes it lie down and it never domes.
scenarios.expect: reject: it must dome within a few ticks of the hit; lying down at once and doming an hour later is the 'simply lies down when hurt' false pass, not a dome triggered by the heat hit

scenarios.text: On three deep-ash pads under the per-cell fertility probe, the wet fresh scar reads about 190%, the dry fresh scar about 90%, and wet old ash about 140% while the black rain lasts. The dry fresh scar's bonus is gone by day 6. The black rain is held on over the wet fresh scar, and on day 9 that pad still reads about 190%.
scenarios.expect: reject: the burn bonus must fall to zero by day 6 to 7 on its own clock, rain or no rain; on the wet pad the rain is keeping it alive (a bonus that does not fade)

scenarios.text: Map-wide scorch-fruit count is zero at the start. The burn line crosses a deep-ash pad and scorch-fruit comes up on burning and smoking cells right behind the front. The unburned control pad, laid on a patch of ordinary soil set down for the test beside the field, has none. A colonist picks the ripe fruit and a hungry colonist eats it; an unpicked plant withers within a day and the stack rots in about four days.
scenarios.expect: reject: the unburned control must be the same Pyrelands ground and age; a control on non-Pyrelands soil refuses scorch-fruit for another reason, so 'never on unburned ground' is not shown

control.note: Control reader got the tree with the leaf removed and its sheet lines dropped; it accepted e1 and c1 (a bite with no venom; a control bite that also leaves venom), which both real Readers reject, so the scenarios discriminate.

readerA.why: A flamefang bite leaving only a wound with no venom on the health tab is the leaf's red.
The drop cell sits next to a cell the front had already reached, so it matches the false pass of the cell being lit by the fire's own spread rather than a new fire ahead of the blaze.
The burned pad's loose ash equals what the unburned pad banked from drift, which is the false pass of ambient drift that would have banked there without any fire.
The running game's def shows body size 2.4 and the beast is muffalo-sized, so it fails the live size 6 bar; the false pass says size must not be read from the XML.
Live body size 6, a warmth status next to the beast and absent far away, and a sheltered room hotter than its twin with no fire nearby meet the oracle.
Lying down like any hurt animal with the dome sprite drawn all the time are both listed false passes.
The front burns out and nothing relights through day five, which is the leaf's red.
Donor animals and plants on the map, with big predators outnumbering grazers, is the leaf's red.
A two-cell vanilla strip stops the front and a near-side relight, a hawk ember lights six cells past it, and there is no chemfuel firebreak floor, all as the leaf promises.
About 25% green on day 3 and 60% on day 7 without replanting, with open ground carpeted, meets the card thresholds.
A rained-on fresh scar reading no better than wet old ash is the leaf's red (black rain wiping the bonus).
Scorch-fruit comes up in the fresh scar right behind the front and not on unburned ash, feeds a colonist and rots fast.
Black rain drawing as blue-grey ordinary rain is the leaf's red.
Ordinary rain still on the biome's weather list, even at low commonality, is the leaf's red.
A herd that arrived on its own drifts to the two-day-old burn and passes over both the fresh scar and the unburned grass, as the leaf requires.
Five glass sand per cell, gravel left behind, no second dig, and a reachable non-sand cell that refuses the order meet the oracle.
The warg control also shows RM_FlamefangVenom, which is the false pass of any bite applying the venom.
The scenario calls for clear weather, but this burn ran under ash fall, and the burned pad holds only 3 more loose ash than the ash-dusting-off control, so almost all of it is ambient drift.
The live def reads body size 3.2, the classic value rather than 6, and the drawn size alone does not count; the size must come from the running game's def.
The oracle wants the dome with the burrow job within a few ticks of the hit, not lying down at once and doming an hour later (the false pass of simply lying down when hurt).
The bonus must fade by day 6 to 7 rain or no rain, but the wet fresh scar still reads 190% on day 9, so it reads as a bonus that never fades.
The unburned control sits on ordinary soil rather than the same ground, which is the listed false pass of a control that refuses the fruit for another reason.

readerB.why: A flamefang bite leaving only a wound and no venom entry is the leaf's red.
The front's spread had already reached the next cell, so the drop cell may have been lit by the fire's own spread, which is a listed false pass, and it was not lit ahead of the front.
The burned pad's loose ash matches the unburned pad's, so it is ambient drift that would have banked there without any fire, a listed false pass.
The running game's def reads 2.4 and the beast is muffalo-sized; the size must come from the live def, and an ordinary-sized beast is the red.
The live body size is 6 and the beast is drawn as a giant; with no fire nearby, warmth shows beside it and not away from it, and its room is hotter than its twin.
An animal that simply lies down when hurt, with the dome sprite drawn the whole time, matches both of the leaf's false passes.
The front burns once and the map stays without fire through day five, which is the leaf's red.
Donor animals and plants are on the map and predators outnumber grazers, which is the red.
The two-cell paved strip stops both the front and a near-side relight, the hawk's ember six cells past is allowed, and the firebreak floor is gone.
About 25% green on day 3 and 60% on day 7 without replanting meets the card thresholds, and the ground is carpeted with no bare dirt.
The rained-on fresh scar reads no better than wet old ash, which is the red: black rain wiped the bonus.
The fruit comes up within hours behind the front and none on unburned ash; it feeds a colonist and rots fast.
Black rain drawn as blue-grey ordinary rain is the leaf's red.
Ordinary rain on the biome's weather list is the red, even if it was never chosen.
The herd arrived on its own and went to the two-day-old burn, passing the fresh scar and the unburned grass alike.
Five glass sand per cell, the cell turns to gravel, there is no second dig, and a reachable non-sand control refuses the order.
The warg control's bite also applies RM_FlamefangVenom, so any bite applies the venom, a listed false pass.
With ash-dusting off the pad still holds 35 of the 38 loose ash, so nearly all of it is ambient drift and not ash the fire left.
The live def reads 3.2, the classic size and not 6; the giant look comes from draw size, and only the XML says 6, a listed false pass.
The ashwallow lay down at once and only domed about an hour later, but the oracle requires the dome within a few ticks; lying down when hurt is a false pass.
The wet fresh scar still reads 190% on day 9, so the bonus never fades on its six-day clock rain or no rain, which the leaf disallows.
The unburned control is on ordinary soil, not Pyrelands ground, which is a listed false pass.

The burned pad's loose ash equals the drift on the unburned pad, which is the false pass 'ambient drift that would have banked there without any fire'.
The leaf requires body size 6 in the running game and must not read as a muffalo-sized beast, but the live def shows 2.4.

The dome showing all the time and the animal just lying down when hurt are both listed false passes.
No relight anywhere through day five matches the red: it burns once and the map holds no fire by day three.
Donor plants and animals on the map, and predators outnumbering grazers, are the leaf's red.
